content: Ligand 2 is an aminophenyl thioether pyrazole and ligand 1 an oxadiazole-benzofuran; both are inactive and neither has anything worth crossing over. Ligand 1 does have a terminal methoxy methyl at atom 0 over an acyclic bond, which is the anchor that keeps one carbon and discards the other 16. The molecule I want to rebuild first has no methyl in it, so I cannot reach it in a single call from this host - but I can get there in two. This step attaches the whole pharmacophore to the surviving methyl, giving the acetanilide form: a conjugated anilide N-H on a benzene, meta to an arylamine N-H whose pyridine carries a bromine at C4. That is the arrangement three runs have converged on, with the bromine being the discovery that ended the last run. The acetyl is only a placeholder; I will swap it for a cyclopropyl next, which is worth about 0.10 of activity over an acetyl and has the best synthetic accessibility of any cap I have measured.
